Prathankarnpap/Shutterstock 17.11.2026 15:00 Society By Athanasia Akrivou Share Workers are due to benefit from two major changes next year: lower income tax withholding for employees with three children from January 1 and a minimum wage increase and reduced social security contributions from April 1
 Μake us preferred on Google Two dates will be important for workers’ paychecks in 2027: January 1, when employees with three dependent children who pay income tax will begin benefiting from lower tax withholding, and April 1, when the minimum wage is expected to rise and private-sector social security contributions are set to fall by half a percentage point. If the proposed increase takes the gross monthly minimum wage from €920 to €960, a 23-year-old employee with no recognized seniority increments could receive approximately €39 more per month after accounting for the reduction in social security contributions. The final minimum wage will be determined through the legally prescribed process. January 1: Tax relief for employees with three children
 The first change will affect salaried workers with three dependent children. Starting with the 2027 tax year, the income tax rate on the first €20,000 of taxable income will fall to zero. Combined with the tax credit available to salaried employees, this will raise the annual income threshold below which no income tax is due from €14,364 to approximately €25,364. Employees who currently pay income tax will see the difference reflected in their January paychecks through lower withholding. NEWSLETTER TABLE TALK

At taxable income of €30,000, the annual tax reduction will reach €1,800. Private-sector employees who benefit from the new tax scale will receive an additional gain in April, when their social security contributions are also scheduled to decrease. April 1: Minimum wage and contribution changes
 The gross monthly minimum wage for full-time employment currently stands at €920. Under the proposed scenario of a €40 increase, it would rise to €960, a gain of 4.35%. At the same time, the employee social security contribution rate in the private sector is expected to drop from 13.37% to 12.87%. Taking both changes into account, the monthly take-home pay of a 23-year-old employee with no recognized seniority increments would increase from approximately €797 to €836. Workers earning the minimum wage who have recognized years of service will also benefit, as their seniority increments are calculated on the basis of the new minimum wage. For employees entitled to three three-year seniority increments, gross monthly earnings would rise from €1,196 to €1,248 if the minimum wage reaches €960. The same increase would also be reflected in the public-sector pay scales, adding €40 gross per month. How much workers will save on social security contributions
 The planned reduction in contributions will also benefit private-sector employees earning more than the minimum wage. The monthly savings will depend on gross earnings: €1,500 gross salary: €7.50 less in monthly contributions.
 €2,000 gross salary: €10 less per month.
 €3,000 gross salary: €15 less per month.
 The changes will therefore affect workers across different salary levels, while employees with three dependent children in the private sector could benefit from both the January tax relief and the April reduction in social security contributions. minimum wage
